entries.text: Purpose knowledge-mcp is a globally-installable MCP server and CLI tool. It maintains a directory of structured markdown files and an file in each software project so AI agents read curated intent and decisions instead of raw source code, reducing token cost and improving plan quality. Agents also gain self-correction capability through the tool, which runs project-specific verification commands without human intervention.

Decisions - Dual interface : MCP server (primary, stdio transport) + CLI (secondary). Both share core modules. routes by argv: no args or → MCP mode; any other subcommand → CLI mode. - Dual model routing : Claude API for initial full-codebase generation (structural, expensive, one-shot). Ollama for incremental per-module updates (fast, local, zero marginal cost). See . - JSON vector store : Embeddings persisted as . No extra services. chromadb is the named upgrade path. See . - Project-local knowledge : lives in the project repo alongside source code. No central server.

Patterns MCP server is always invoked in stdio mode. Working directory ( ) determines which project's is used. Config is loaded once at startup from . Project artifacts managed per-project: - — project root; auto-loaded by AI agents at session start - — structured docs; read via MCP tools - — current implementation task; written by tool - — vector index; managed by search engine

Constraints - is reserved for MCP stdio protocol. All diagnostics/logs go to . - Files writable by MCP tools: , , any file under . Never write outside these. - Config is global ( ). Knowledge is local (project ). - MCP tools that mutate state: , , , . - MCP tools that are read-only: , , .

Tech Stack - TypeScript 5, Node 20, (ESM) - — MCP server and stdio transport - — Claude API - — CLI argument parsing - — config and tool-input validation - Native — Ollama HTTP calls (no extra dependency)
Purpose Coding standards for the knowledge-mcp TypeScript codebase. These are non-negotiable.

Patterns - ESM imports with extension : . TypeScript under resolves imports to source files at compile time. - Zod at system boundaries only : Validate all MCP tool inputs and config file data with Zod. Internal functions receive already-typed values. - Named exports only : No default exports. One barrel per directory that re-exports the public API. Internal helpers are not exported from barrels. - Typed errors : Throw (extends ) with a typed field. MCP handlers catch and return . CLI handlers catch and write to , then .

Decisions - No sync fs : All file I/O via . Sync methods forbidden. - No : Use at boundaries; narrow with Zod or type guards. - No : MCP uses stdout for wire-format protocol bytes. Use for all debug output. - Types inferred from Zod : . Do not write parallel TypeScript interfaces for Zod-validated data.

Constraints - File names: kebab-case ( ). - Function names: camelCase. Types/interfaces: PascalCase. Constants: SCREAMING SNAKE CASE. - Indentation: 2 spaces. No tabs. No trailing whitespace. - Do not use CommonJS ( , ). - Do not define types inline in implementation files — all shared types live in .

Format — one backtick-wrapped command per bullet: - Add more commands as the project grows (e.g. , ). Commands run in the project working directory captured at MCP server startup.

Context What problem or situation prompted this decision? What forces or constraints were in play?

Decision Use a plain JSON file ( ) as the vector store for semantic search indexing.

Context Semantic search requires storing embedding vectors and querying them by similarity. Options evaluated: - chromadb — well-featured, but requires a running server or SQLite native bindings - sqlite-vss — native binary module, platform-specific build issues - hnswlib-node — native binary, ANN search, overkill for this scale - Plain JSON + in-memory cosine — zero dependencies, works anywhere Node runs

Rationale Knowledge bases are small by design (dozens to 200 sections at most). Linear cosine scan over all vectors in JS takes <10ms at this scale. A plain JSON file requires no additional dependencies, is human-readable, inspectable with , and travels with the project in git.

Upgrade Path If a project's knowledge base grows beyond 1,000 sections (e.g., a large monorepo), replace with a chromadb implementation behind the same / / interface. The search engine ( ) and all callers require no changes.

Consequences - Zero extra dependencies or native binaries. - Index is human-readable and version-controllable. - Linear scan is unsuitable past 1,000 entries — but that's well beyond the expected use case. - Full index rebuild required after any knowledge update (acceptable for batch usage).
Decision Use the Claude API for initial full-codebase knowledge generation; use Ollama (local model) for incremental per-module updates.

Context Two operations have fundamentally different characteristics: 1. Initial generation ( ): Reads potentially large amounts of source code across many files, requires structural reasoning about the whole codebase, runs once (or rarely after major refactors). 2. Incremental update ( ): Looks at a handful of changed files, regenerates one module doc, runs frequently (after each PR or commit batch).

Rationale Claude excels at structural reasoning over large contexts — exactly what initial generation needs. But calling Claude for every incremental update costs money and introduces network latency for an operation that should feel instant. A 7B code model (e.g., ) running locally via Ollama handles "here are the changed files, update this module doc" adequately with zero marginal cost and sub-second response time.

Consequences - Ollama must be running locally for and . - An Anthropic API key is required only for — all other operations work without one. - Two models to configure, but sensible defaults handle the common case. - The quality gap for incremental updates (7B vs Claude) is acceptable because module docs are small, structured, and the model has the current doc as a reference to update from.
Decision Standardize all files with a YAML-like frontmatter block followed by fixed -level section headings.

Context AI agents reading these files need to locate specific kinds of information (interfaces, constraints, usage patterns) without reading entire files. The reader module needs to extract metadata (module name, source files list) for filtering and staleness detection. The updater model needs a consistent template to regenerate any file from the same prompt.
Format ``` --- module: <name (required) updated: <YYYY-MM-DD (required) files: [list of source files this covers] ---

Section Semantics - — one paragraph: what this module does and why it exists - — bullets of non-obvious choices made and why; alternatives rejected - — how to use this correctly; code examples where helpful - — do/don't rules; start each bullet with "Do not", "Never", or "Always" - — key exported types and function signatures; no implementation details - — which source files this module covers and what each does

Consequences - Agents can request specific sections by name. - The updater model can regenerate any file using the same prompt template. - Not all sections are required — omit sections with no meaningful content rather than writing placeholder text. - Reader can be implemented with a trivial regex parser (no YAML library needed).
Decision Pass from to , and call inside .

Context Commander's default behavior (the default) assumes it receives the full array — with the binary and script path as the first two elements — and strips them internally. If pre-slices the array and also uses the default behavior, Commander strips two more elements and loses the subcommand name entirely. All CLI subcommands silently fall through to the help screen with no error. Two valid approaches exist: 1. Pass the full (unsliced) to and let Commander strip internally. 2. Pre-slice in (which already inspects to decide MCP vs CLI mode) and tell Commander not to strip via . Option 2 was chosen so receives exactly the args it needs with no implicit stripping dependency on the caller.

Rationale makes the contract explicit: always receives a pre-sliced array (no binary path, no script path), and Commander respects that. Option 1 would make implicitly depend on receiving a full -shaped array, which is a hidden contract that breaks if the caller ever changes.

Consequences - always receives — never the full . - Do NOT change back to — the option is load-bearing; removing it silently breaks all subcommands. - Do NOT pass the full (unsliced) to — that would also cause double-stripping under the current setup.
Decision Generate in the project root as part of , and surface it automatically in (no-arg call) via the MCP tool handler.

Context AI coding agents (Claude Code, Zed, Cursor, GitHub Copilot Workspace) auto-load files named , , or from the project root at session start. This gives them orientation — project purpose, build commands, key constraints — before any user message or tool call. Without this file, an agent landing in a knowledge-mcp-managed project must call explicitly to get oriented, which requires prior knowledge that the tool exists. With AGENTS.md in the root, agents get baseline context for free, then call for depth. Two design questions arose: 1. Where does the file live? Root vs inside . 2. Where do verification commands come from? A new config key vs reading from .

Rationale Root placement : Agents auto-load from the project root, not subdirectories. Placing AGENTS.md in would make it just another knowledge file — it would not be auto-loaded. The whole point is zero-tool-call context injection. Verification commands from : The section of is already the natural home for "how to check this project is correct" — that is a coding convention. Adding a separate config key ( or a new ) would fragment information that belongs together. The tool reads from so there is a single source of truth. Auto-injection in (no-arg) : When an agent calls with no arguments to get a full project context dump, it should also receive AGENTS.md content — even if the agent already auto-loaded the file, it may have been truncated. Injecting it here is free and ensures completeness. This belongs in the MCP tool handler ( ), not in , because AGENTS.md has no frontmatter and is not a .

Consequences - grows by one file: at the project root. Same idempotency rules apply. - gains a section listing shell commands. The format is a markdown bullet list of backtick-wrapped commands. - parses the section from at call time (not cached), so changes to the section take effect immediately without restarting the server. - with no args becomes the "full context" call: all knowledge files + AGENTS.md. Agents should prefer this on session start.
Purpose <one sentence from architecture.md Purpose, or placeholder

Decisions - Project root, not inside : Agents auto-load files from the project root. Placing it inside would require an explicit tool call to discover it. Root placement gives zero-cost context injection before any tool use. - Pointers over content : AGENTS.md does not duplicate knowledge — it points to and tells agents to call first. Duplication causes drift; pointers stay correct. - Verification commands inline : The build/verify commands are repeated here from so agents can run them without a separate read call. This is the one intentional duplication, justified by access frequency. - Generated by , not : produces knowledge files from source code via Claude. AGENTS.md is structural scaffolding — always the same shape, just parameterized by project name. It belongs with .
Patterns Template structure (in order, no blank sections): ```markdown <project-name
Knowledge Base This project uses knowledge-mcp. Read before writing code. Start every session: call with no arguments.
Build & Verify <bullet list of commands from Verification in conventions.md, or placeholders
Key Constraints <bullet list of the 3–5 most critical constraints from architecture.md and conventions.md ```

Constraints - must not overwrite an existing . Same idempotency rule as all other init files. - is written to directly (the project root), not inside . - Do not use to write — that function targets . Use directly to . - Content must stay under 60 lines. Agents load this before any tool call; bloating it wastes context. - When the MCP tool is called with no arguments, the handler appends AGENTS.md content to the response if the file exists. This is handled in , not in — AGENTS.md has no frontmatter and is not a .
Interfaces AGENTS.md is not a TypeScript interface — it is a file written by . No exported function is specific to it; it is produced as part of the init file list.

Purpose Commander.js CLI entrypoint. Maps subcommands ( , , , , ) to core module functions. Handles human-readable output to stdout and errors to stderr. is the universal entrypoint that routes to either the MCP server or the CLI.

Decisions - as universal entrypoint : If is , , or absent, start the MCP server (MCP clients invoke the binary with no args; / are explicit aliases). Any other value is routed to the CLI module. - CLI imports nothing from : calls via routing, not a direct import. This prevents CLI from pulling in MCP server code unnecessarily. - Config loaded in : Both paths (MCP and CLI) need config. Load it once in , pass to whichever path is taken. - with Ollama : Calls to get the target module, reads its source files, calls with a regeneration prompt, writes the result back.

Purpose Initializes the MCP server, registers all seven tools with their input schemas and handlers, and connects to stdio transport. Tool handlers delegate to core modules (knowledge-io, search, scaffold).

Decisions - handles all seven tools : is wiring only ( , , ). Keeping tools together makes the tool surface easy to audit. - captured at startup : is resolved once when the server starts. MCP clients cannot change the working directory mid-session. - Zod validation inside each handler : Each handler parses through its Zod schema before any logic. Invalid input returns , never throws. - API : Uses + from . Tool input schemas are expressed as JSON Schema objects (not Zod — MCP protocol requires JSON Schema).

Patterns — Tool Behaviours — when called with no argument, returns all knowledge files AND the contents of (project root) if it exists. AGENTS.md is appended after the knowledge files in the response. This makes the no-arg call the canonical "full project context" call for agents starting a session. When a filter is provided, AGENTS.md is not included. — reads the section from , extracts each ` <command child process.exec Verification verify project { type: 'object', properties: {} }` — no parameters.

Constraints - Never write to in any tool handler. MCP transport owns stdout. - All tool handlers must be non-throwing: catch all errors, return . - Tool names are exact: , , , , , , . - uses (promisified), not . The handler must be async and await each command. Commands time out after 60 seconds each. - does not shell-escape commands — they are taken verbatim from conventions.md. Conventions.md is a trusted project file, not user input.

Purpose HTTP client for Ollama's REST API. Two operations: generates an embedding vector for a text string (used by the search engine), and produces a text completion (used by ). Uses native — no SDK dependency.

Decisions - No Ollama SDK : The two endpoints used ( , ) are stable and simple. A thin client avoids a dependency and works with any Ollama version. - for generate : Simplifies implementation. Knowledge updates are offline/batch; streaming latency is not a benefit. - Factory function pattern : returns an object. Config is closed over — callers don't thread config through every call.

Constraints - Embed timeout: 30 seconds via . - Generate timeout: 120 seconds via . - On any non-2xx response or network error, throw . - Do not retry. The caller decides retry policy. - Never log request bodies — they may contain proprietary source code.

Purpose Semantic search across the knowledge base. Chunks each knowledge file into sections (split by headings), generates embeddings via Ollama, stores them in the JSON vector index, and returns top-N results by cosine similarity.

Decisions - Section-level chunking at boundaries : Sections are semantically coherent and small enough for accurate embedding. Splitting at heading boundaries avoids mixing unrelated content in one chunk. - Lazy index rebuild on staleness : On each search, compare mtime against all file mtimes. If any is newer, rebuild before searching. First-time search with no index also triggers rebuild. - In-process cosine similarity : At knowledge-base scale (dozens to 200 sections), linear scan over all vectors in JS is fast (<10ms). No ANN library needed.

Constraints - If Ollama is unreachable, throw . Never return empty results silently. - Strip markdown formatting (code fences, backticks, chars) from section text before embedding. Store stripped text in the index. - Index rebuild writes to then atomically renames to . - Sections shorter than 20 characters after stripping are skipped.
Files - — , , , staleness check, markdown stripper, section chunker

Purpose Persists and retrieves the vector index as . Provides CRUD operations for vector entries. Acts as the storage layer beneath the search engine — the search engine calls these functions; nothing else does.

Decisions - Plain JSON, no compression : Inspectable with any text editor, zero dependencies. At knowledge-base scale, JSON serialization overhead is negligible. - Version field = 1 : enables future schema migrations without breaking existing reads. - Deterministic entry IDs : . Deterministic IDs enable to overwrite stale entries by key. - is pure : Takes an index and new entries, returns a new index. Does not write to disk. Callers call afterward.

Constraints - Index path is always . Never configurable. - returns if file does not exist — never throws. - is the only place that writes . Do not write the file anywhere else. - Do not store full markdown in entries — only store stripped plain text.

Purpose Instructions for the coding model implementing knowledge-mcp from PLAN.md. The coding model has access to PLAN.md and the directory only — no other context.

Before writing any code 1. Read completely. Understand the full file inventory and implementation order before touching anything. 2. Read for the system shape and data flow. 3. Read — these rules are non-negotiable. 4. For each file you are about to implement, read its module doc in .

Implementation rules - Implement in the order given in PLAN.md . Dependencies must compile before dependents. - first : All shared interfaces, the class, , and type live here. Do not define types inline in implementation files. - Match interface contracts exactly : Function signatures in each module's section are contracts. Do not rename, add, or remove parameters without updating the module doc. - No stdout in library code : Any debug output goes to . This is critical — MCP server mode uses stdout for the protocol wire format. - ESM imports : Every local import uses extension: . This is required for Node ESM under . - Shebang in : The very first line of must be . - Zod schemas define types : Use for any Zod-validated data shape. Do not write a parallel TypeScript interface.
After each file Run to check for type errors before moving to the next file. Fix all errors before proceeding.
When you encounter ambiguity Search with or for the relevant concept. If no guidance exists, prefer the simplest implementation that satisfies the declared interface.
Purpose Instructions for an AI planning agent using the knowledge base to plan features or changes to knowledge-mcp.

How to plan a feature 1. Read architecture first : Call with no filter. Study the data flow diagram and the constraints section — they define what is possible and what is forbidden. 2. Identify affected modules : For the feature, determine which modules are relevant. Read each with . Note the section — these are the integration contracts you must respect. 3. Search for prior patterns : Use with the feature concept (e.g., , ) to surface relevant sections without reading all files. 4. Check decision records : Read files. A decision may directly constrain or validate your approach. 5. Write the plan : Call to output a PLAN.md with: - Files to create or modify (with purpose) - Any new interfaces or type changes to - Implementation order (topological — dependencies before dependents) - Any new dependencies and why

Anti-patterns - Do not plan changes that violate constraints in (e.g., writing to stdout from library code, creating files outside ). - Do not add dependencies without documenting why existing facilities are insufficient. - Do not create a new module without a corresponding entry in the plan. - Do not design for hypothetical future requirements — solve the stated problem only.
Purpose Instructions for updating module files after source code changes. Called by the MCP tool or the CLI command.

entries.id: skills/updater::When to update a module doc
entries.section: When to update a module doc
entries.text: When to update a module doc Update when: - A function signature in the module changes (added param, changed return type). - A new constraint is discovered or an existing one is removed. - A significant usage pattern is added or changed. - New source files are added to the module. - The module is split or merged with another. Do not update for pure internal refactors that leave the module's external interface and behavior unchanged.

How to update 1. Read the current to understand the existing doc. 2. Read the changed source files listed in plus any newly added files. 3. Identify exactly what changed: interfaces, patterns, constraints, file list. 4. Rewrite only the affected sections. Copy unchanged sections verbatim. 5. Update the frontmatter date to today. 6. Call to persist the updated doc.

After updating Verify: does the section still reflect current exported function signatures exactly? If not, fix it before saving. After saving, the search engine will lazily rebuild the vector index on the next call.

Format rules - Keep each file under 400 words. - bullets must start with "Do not", "Never", or "Always". - shows only exported symbols — no private helpers, no implementation details. - Use triple-backtick code blocks with language hint for all code. - Frontmatter array lists only source files that are part of this module's implementation.
